thread:
devon: Heads-up — autoscaler tried to trim 3 GPU nodes in us-west1b this morning and a few PDBs got short-lived evictions.
maya: saw the alerts. which nodepool and instance type?
devon: gpu-pool-preempt (A100-preemptible). scaleDownCandidates list showed 3 nodes, ca started drainage around 08:03 UTC.
ops-bot: cluster-autoscaler: ScaleDown: candidates: [node-uw1b-gpu-12, node-uw1b-gpu-7, node-uw1b-gpu-3] reason: underutilized
li: any pods stuck in Terminating or restarted jobs?
andrew: two training jobs restarted — they were using best-effort priorityclass. logs show quick eviction then reschedule to other nodes.
lisa-oncall: cost note — preemptible pool is cheaper but we need safer drains for longer jobs. We should avoid evicting PDB-protected services.
maya: quick checklist idea: (1) mark long-running training pods with redwood/avoid-preempt: "true", (2) add PDBs for controllers that mustn’t be 0, (3) ensure priorityClass for critical infra pods is high.
devon: we already have priorityclass redwood-critical with value 100000. but many user jobs use default or gpu-batch.
li: proposal: annotate training jobs with priorityClassName: gpu-batch-high (value 50000) and add a PDB for the trainer service if it runs as a statefulset.
andrew: also consider annotation to the nodepool to add a scaleDownGracePeriod label so CA waits longer on that pool.
maya: example PDB for trainer service:
```
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: trainer-pdb
  namespace: ml
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: trainer
```
li: and for short-term mitigation we can set the CA flag --max-graceful-termination-sec and annotate pods with "cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict": "false" for critical ones.
devon: careful — CA respects that annotation only when configured; also kubelet eviction vs PDBs interactions are tricky.
lisa-oncall: immediate action: I added a temporary PDB for the trainer ReplicaSet and bumped priorityClass for infra-exporter to redwood-critical. Watching for next scale event.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: patch applied to ml/trainer: pod disruption budget trainer-pdb created by lisa-oncall at 2026-11-03T08:20:19Z
maya: follow-up: we should update runbook with exact commands. Draft commands I used:
```
kubectl apply -f trainer-pdb.yaml -n ml
kubectl patch pod -n ml <pod> -p '{"metadata": {"annotations": {"cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict": "false"}}}'
```
devon: long-term: consider adding a tiered nodepool strategy: preemptible for ephemeral hyper-burst jobs, reserved pool for long-running checkpoints with a smaller autoscaler buffer.
andrew: also re-evaluate CA scale-down thresholds for gpu pools: increase utilization threshold from 0.5 -> 0.65 for gpu-pool-preempt.
li: we'll open a PR to ops runbooks and schedule a quick retro with ML infra to align on priorityClass naming.
lisa-oncall: monitoring: added a dashboard panel for PDB eviction counts and CA scale-downs against nodepool tags.
maya: thanks — will follow up on PR. tagging @oncall for visibility: @lisa-oncall :eyes:
devon: cool, closing this thread once PR is up. :thumbsup:
